subject: Q about a simulation study with occu in unmarked

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Q about a simulation study with occu in unmarked
parts:
Dear all,

 

With a colleague we are planning a simulation study to explore some features of the estimates of a simple static occupancy model as we vary the values of psi and p between 0.1 and 0.9. In some pilot runs with function occu()  in unmarked we have had quite a number of numerical failures where typically one or more SE’s in a model run were given as either NaN or an NA. We have tried to filter them out and rerun those cases.

 

There are two things we are unsure about:

  1. We were wondering about some general criterion to diagnose a numerical failure, in particular also for those where the SE is estimated at some very large value (e.g., 10 or 100 or more) ?
  2. We are also unsure whether repeating cases with numerical failures as just described is a good idea. After all, these will just be a feature of some combinations of the factors of our simulation (e.g., when psi or p are very small, leading to boundary estimates). Thus, it may be better to tally up the number of such numerical failures and report them as one of the results of our study ?

 

Thanks for comments and ideas.

 

Bestr regards  --- Marc
